name: Crete

accommodation.name: Alma Natura Villas With Sea View
accommodation.details: Villa with kitchen, sea view. Check-in 4:00 PM, check-out 11:00 AM.

vibe: Omid + Annika + Friend (arriving separately, likes structure). Villa with kitchen, Audi Q2. Mix of beach days and road-tripping. One cooking night.

activities.name: Chania old town
activities.description: Venetian Harbor, lighthouse walk, Topanas quarter, Agora market. Multiple visits.

activities.name: Samaria Gorge
activities.description: Europe's longest gorge, 16 km, 4-7 hrs. Open May-Oct. Entry ~$11. Exit at Agia Roumeli, ferry to Sfakion. Start by 7:30am, carry 2+ liters water.

activities.name: Manousakis Winery
activities.description: Western Crete's standout winery. Rhone varieties in Cretan limestone. Terroir Tasting ~$9/pp, Premium ~$17/pp. Taverna on-site. Closed Sundays. Call +30 2821 078787.

restaurants.name: Dounias
restaurants.location: Drakona village (1 hr south via Theriso Gorge)
restaurants.vibe: Mountain taverna. Wood fire, copper pots, no menu — chef serves whatever's ready from his farm. NYT featured. Plan a half-day around this. Closed Tuesdays.

restaurants.name: Tamam
restaurants.vibe: In a converted Ottoman hammam (built ~1400). Since 1982. Traditional Greek with Ottoman-Eastern Med inflections.

restaurants.name: Thalassino Ageri
restaurants.vibe: Tables in the sand facing the lighthouse at sunset. Kakavia (fisherman's soup), sea urchin salad. Most romantic dinner in Chania.

restaurants.name: To Maridaki
restaurants.vibe: Point-at-the-cabinet daily-catch taverna. Simple, perfect fried fish. 4.6/5 from 5,000+ reviews.

restaurants.name: Glossitses
restaurants.vibe: Traditional Cretan home cooking in a garden. Lamb with wild greens, dakos salad.

restaurants.name: Papadakis
restaurants.vibe: Big portions, legendary grilled octopus. Good stop after a beach day.

restaurants.name: Chrisostomos
restaurants.vibe: Family-run, wood-fired traditional Cretan. Genuine local atmosphere at fair prices.

restaurants.name: Salis
restaurants.vibe: Chania's top modern creative restaurant. Cretan organic produce, award-winning wines, stylish but not stiff.

restaurants.name: Steria
restaurants.vibe: 2025 newcomer. Cretan produce + live fire + zero-waste. Cutting-edge rather than traditional.

restaurants.name: Avli
restaurants.vibe: 15th-century Venetian mansion, bougainvillea courtyard. 460-wine enoteca. Worth the drive for a special dinner.

restaurants.name: Avli Raw Materials
restaurants.vibe: Casual sibling of Avli. Wine bar meets deli. More approachable for daytime.

bars.name: Monastiri
bars.vibe: Cocktail bar in ruins of a Venetian monastery. Lighthouse-view terrace. Cretan spirits and ingredients.

bars.name: Fagotto Jazz Bar
bars.vibe: Greece's first jazz bar, since 1977. 15th-century Venetian building. Live jazz/blues every evening from 9pm.

bars.name: Sinagogi
bars.vibe: Open-air summer bar in an old synagogue courtyard. Stone walls, candlelit. Cocktails, occasional DJ. Open Jun-Sep.

bars.name: Pallas Rooftop
bars.vibe: Rooftop with harbor views in a Venetian building. Refined sundowners.

beaches.name: Balos Lagoon
beaches.vibe: The famous turquoise lagoon. No shade — bring everything. Go early (fills by 10am). Book the Kissamos ferry online if taking the boat (~$45/pp, capacity-controlled in 2026). The Q2 handles the dirt road.

beaches.name: Falassarna
beaches.vibe: Wide golden sand, swimmable, beach tavernas. Best combined with Balos (20 min apart). Wilder north end (Pacheia Ammos) has dunes, no sunbeds, ancient harbor ruins.

beaches.name: Elafonissi
beaches.vibe: Pink-tinged sand, shallow lagoon. Stunning but arrive before 9am in July or parking is a nightmare.

beaches.name: Kedrodasos
beaches.driveTime: Same drive as Elafonissi + 20-min coastal walk
beaches.vibe: Hidden beach with ancient cedar trees growing to the waterline. Natural shade, minimal crowds. No facilities. Bring water and food.

beaches.name: Seitan Limania
beaches.vibe: Dramatic fjord-like inlet between limestone cliffs. Turquoise. Parking fills by 9am. Steep rocky access — not for everyone.

beaches.name: Stavros
beaches.vibe: Where they filmed Zorba the Greek. Sheltered bay, dramatic cliff backdrop. Village tavernas. Zero tourist-trap energy. Easy morning beach.

beaches.name: Marathi
beaches.vibe: Sheltered double cove, tavernas on the sand. Easy, swimmable, low-key.

beaches.name: Loutro
beaches.vibe: Roadless fishing village — only accessible by boat or foot. White buildings, turquoise bay. Swim off rocks, eat at waterfront tavernas. ANENDYK ferry from Sfakion: ~$11, hourly in summer, first ~9:30am, last ~6:45pm.

dayTrips.name: Balos + Falassarna
dayTrips.highlights: Lagoon morning, beach afternoon. Pack water/sunscreen.

dayTrips.name: South coast: Sfakion + Loutro
dayTrips.highlights: Drive 1.5 hrs south through White Mountains (the descent from Imbros is Crete's most dramatic road). Ferry to roadless Loutro. Swim, eat, do nothing.

dayTrips.name: Dounias + Theriso Gorge
dayTrips.highlights: Drive south through the stunning Theriso Gorge to Drakona village (~1 hr). Lunch at Dounias. The gorge road itself is spectacular.

dayTrips.name: Rethymno
dayTrips.highlights: Most intact Venetian old town in Crete. 16th-century Fortezza fortress. Avli for dinner.

dayTrips.name: Imbros Gorge + Sfakion
dayTrips.highlights: 11 km, 2.5-4 hrs, ~$6 entry. Much easier than Samaria, equally scenic. Exit at Komitades, taxi back to car (~$17). Continue to Sfakion for Loutro ferry.

cookingNight.title: Villa Cooking Night
cookingNight.market: Chania Agora (cross-shaped neoclassical market, Minoos Street, Mon-Sat mornings)
shoppingList: Fish from the western portico fishmongers (go 7-9am): sea bream, red mullet, sardines, octopus
Graviera (aged hard cheese — Crete's best), anthotyro (soft fresh)
Cretan olive oil — ask to taste at the stalls
Horta (wild greens) — boil, dress with lemon and olive oil (the real Cretan staple)
Thyme honey for dessert with yogurt
Dried rigani (Cretan oregano, stronger than mainland)
A bottle of Lyrarakis Dafni (white, herbal/bay-leaf character, indigenous grape)
A bottle of Manousakis Nostos (red, Grenache-dominant)
cookingNight.instructions: Grill the fish whole with olive oil and rigani, assemble everything, eat on the villa terrace.

wines.notes: Founded 1966. Rescued nearly extinct indigenous grapes. Fully organic since 2020. Buy at Chania wine shops.
Founded 1930. Clay amphora aging since 2015. Third generation.

wines.signature: Roussanne (one of Greece's best), Nostos blend
wines.notes: Rhone varieties in Cretan soil. Visitable, 30 min from Chania.
Visitable, 30 min from Chania. Organic, solar-powered. Farm-to-table restaurant on-site. Tours at 12/14/17.

bookingPriorities.why: Worth the Rethymno drive, book early
